recipes.name: Tuscan Chard and Cannellini Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 6 cups chicken broth, or more as needed
1 (15 ounce) can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed - or more to taste
1 bunch red or white Swiss chard
0.25 cup uncooked small pasta, such as orzo or pastina

steps.text: Cook onion, bacon, garlic, nutmeg, and pepper flakes in a large saucepan over medium heat until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add chicken broth and cannellini beans; bring to a boil. Stir in cheese rind and sun-dried tomatoes. Reduce heat to a simmer; simmer about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut stems from chard leaves; slice stems into ¾-inch long pieces. Cut chard leaves into 1-inch wide ribbons; set aside. Stir chard stems and pasta into soup. Reduce heat to a simmer; cook until pasta is tender, about 10 minutes. Stir in chard leaves, sage, and basil; simmer until just wilted, 3 to 4 minutes.
Divide soup among bowls. Top with grated cheese; drizzle with olive oil.

raw_recipe.headline: Tuscan Chard and Cannellini Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: This robust, Tuscan chard and cannellini bean soup with pasta recipe comes together in no time. Adding Parmigiano-Reggiano or the rinds lends deeper flavor.

review.reviewBody: Actually, with some changes it is a 10 and I don't feel bad for making some changes and then rating it because the cook herself in her note suggested most of them. I used bulk sausage browned and crumbled instead of bacon, no nutmeg, canned diced tomatoes and a few squirts of tomato paste, basil and italian herbs. I served with fresh grated parmesan, a squeeze of lemon and some garlic croutons. Took me back to my grandmother's table on Sunday afternoon, she was from Naples, had 10 kids and over 40 grandkids and served a lot of beans and greens out of economic necessity. To me it is a gourmet treat.

Loved this soup! Excellent flavors. I made a double batch and the only changes I made were increasing the garlic to 5 cloves (sliced -- not minced) , adding a little extra bacon, and omitting the sage because I didn't have any. I also used about 3/4 lbs. of dry great northern beans, cooked beforehand in a pressure cooker. This is definitely a keeper for my list of ideas to use up a leftover rotisserie chicken.

Kitchen sink recipe!
Meaning a great recipe to adapt (as the writer states) to use up what you have on hand. I found it after doing an ingredient search on the site in order to get rid of some items before I head out of town for the week. Generally followed it.
Used double the bacon, beans, and garlic. Used 1/2 cup ditalini for dried pasta. Used 8 cups chicken broth. I had about 3 oz. of jarred (and seasoned) sun-dried tomatoes to use up, so I drained them and chopped. No swiss chard, but used up some spinach. No fresh sage, but added about a 1/2 tsp of dried ground sage with the nutmeg to cut down on the concentration. Simmered longer to let all of this flavor come together. Overall, really great. Bonus for the traveller: will freeze well in portions and be an awesome meal when I get home! Will adapt really well to personal taste and substitutions for what you have on hand. Highly recommend you try it for yourself as close to the original ingredients as possible, and see for yourself. Thanks.
PS- Obviously, you should serve with crusty bread!

Soup is delicious but I did make a few changes! I used a pound of mild Italian sausage instead of bacon! I eliminated sage and nutmeg. I added one 15 oz. can of diced tomatoes and added about 2 cups of ditalini pasta! I did use a Parmesan cheese rind which definitely added a pleasant cheese flavor to the soup! And my Swiss chard was fresh from my garden! Overall the soup was a big hit and I WILL make it again!!

A very nice quick soup. I would cook the bacon longer, until more crispy next time. I used a 1/4 tsp. Ground nutmeg and 1 tsp. dried sage rather than fresh. Had fresh basil, added a can of Italian diced tomatoes as well as a couple of tablespoons sun dried tomato pesto. I hate it when pasta gets overcooked, blown up, and mushy, so I cooked it separately and then added at the end. It’s worth adding top the recipe book and playing with!

I did not have nutmeg, but i crisped the bacon befor i chopped it. I also added 3 small young shallots to the onoin mix. I Carmelized the whole lot befor adding the broth and beans. only had BetterThan Bullion on hand instead of chicken broth. Same thing really. I should have cut the chard ribbons a bit shorter. I only had dry sage, so i added it early. This is outstanding no matter the variety .

Made again with fresh sage. I think the flavor was better when i used the dry sage that i added earlier. Plus, crisping the bacon and carmelizing the onions before adding the broth is definitely the bestter route if you have the extra time. None tge less, this is an excellent recipe.

I chose this recipe only because I had everything on hand and needing to be used with the exception of the Chard. Am I glad I did1 I did alter/add a few ingredients but I'm sure it would be fine stand alone. Increased the bacon to four slices and fried it by itself and then drained almost all the fat. Added a bit of EVO and sauteed the onion and extra garlic......can't have too much garlic. Increased the sun dried tomatoes to about 1/3 C. The Parmesan rind has to be the key to this recipe. I've seen it on TV but never tried it myself. It gave the soup a wonderful flavor. I think six cups broth is a little shy for soup, if you want it soupy maybe eight cups is better. I used four cups broth but the orzo I used was already cooked and leftover so you need to take that into account. I also increased the basil to about a 1/4C......we like fresh basil! We loved it and will make it again.

Yes did make a few changes, I used a can of fire-roasted tomatoes instead of the sun dried tomatoes. I did not use the bacon as I made this all-vegetarian dish. I also doubled the white cannellini beans to two cans and vegetable broth to six cups, pasta I used 1/2 cup small elbow macaroni.

Used others’ suggestions. I like a soup that’s very chunky so I did not increase the stock. I used Vegeta (Polish vegetable stock). I doubled the pasta, omitted the sage because I don’t care for it. I think the Parmesan rind is an absolute must! If anyone else is wondering How much a bunch really is, I used 9 ounces of red chard leaves and 3 ounces of stem (sorry I forgot to weigh it before I cut everything up so I am stating the amount separately). Could use even more chard to your liking. I used 3 very large fresh Roma tomatoes, 1/2 the nutmeg, and double the beans.

This was pretty good, and with a few tweaks, I think it will be excellent. I ended up doubling the recipe but I didn't have enough beans and bacon but I did have some yellow potatoes and ham. I don't necessarily recommend adding it to the soup. It was fine, but too much of a hodge podge. Next time I plan to use pancetta instead of bacon and crisp that up first and keep it aside as a topping. I may also add a bit of lemon zest right at the end. I will NOT use the sage next time. It didn't add anything and made for a strange aftertaste.

I'm on a low sodium diet so I had to substitute low sodium ingredients for some of the higher sodium ingredients, e.g., I used liquid smoke instead of the bacon, etc., but it came out great anyway. I used fresh rainbow chard from my garden and beans prepared from scratch. This recipe is definitely a keeper and I will make it again and again.
Good stuff. Easy, healthy and filling.
I love this recipe especially if you have fresh herbs and chard. The dried tomato’s are awesome too. I like to brown my bacon more before I add my onions.
Hearty soup with complex flavors! Easy to sub ingredients.

I'm vegan so I made this soup accordingly and my husband and I both loved it! I didn't want to make a trip to the store so used what I had on hand and had to substitute barley for the pasta and dried Italian seasoning in place of the sage and basil. I'll be making this again and again.

I made it without bacon and double beans & pasta YUM

Had soup with Grilled bread with parmesan, garlic, onion, and olive oil
left off the clove and sage and use a can of tomatoes in lieu of sun dried. delish!
I used Kale instead of chard because that is what I had. It was flavorful and tasty. I also used the whole back of bacon.
Yum! Maybe just need to sauté stems & leaves ahead of putting in soup pot.

So I had no idea what cannelini beans were and gave up after three stores didn’t sell them. I substituted white kidney beans and low and behold on the label under the words white kidney beans it said canceling beans! Who knew? 
Lovely taste and my accent sundried tomatoes found a purpose!
